articles.headline: RBI approves record ₹2.11 lakh crore dividend for the central government
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's board approved a record surplus transfer of ₹2,10,874 crore to the Union government for FY24. This is more than double the previous year's payout and significantly exceeds the budget estimate of ₹1.02 lakh crore. The windfall is expected to help the government maintain its fiscal deficit target of 5.1% of GDP while potentially increasing infrastructure spending.

articles.headline: ITC net profit slips 1.3% to ₹5,020 crore in fourth quarter
articles.summary: ITC reported a marginal 1.3% year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit to ₹5,020.20 crore for the quarter ended March 2024. Revenue from operations grew slightly to ₹17,752.87 crore. The company board recommended a final dividend of ₹7.50 per share. Performance was impacted by macro-economic headwinds and a high base effect in the agribusiness segment.

articles.headline: Gautam Adani reclaims Asia's richest person title from Mukesh Ambani
articles.summary: Gautam Adani has overtaken Mukesh Ambani to become the richest person in Asia according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Adani's net worth rose to $111 billion following a surge in the share prices of Adani Group companies. The conglomerate has seen a strong recovery in investor confidence after recent legal and financial clarifications regarding the Hindenburg report allegations.

articles.headline: India manufacturing PMI climbs to 58.4 signaling strong sector growth
articles.summary: The HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rose to 58.4 in May from 57.5 in April. This indicates the strongest improvement in the health of the manufacturing sector since October 2020. The expansion was driven by substantial increases in new orders and output, leading to the fastest rate of job creation in over a decade.

articles.headline: Centre relaxes onion export ban for Maldives and other friendly nations
articles.summary: The Indian government has permitted the export of specific quantities of onions to countries including Maldives, Mauritius, and Sri Lanka under its 'Neighborhood First' policy. While the general export ban remains, these exports will be channeled through the National Cooperative Exports Ltd. The decision aims to support the food security requirements of strategic partner nations.

articles.headline: InterGlobe Aviation reports record annual net profit of ₹8,176 crore
articles.summary: Indigo's parent company, InterGlobe Aviation, reported a net profit of ₹1,894.8 crore for the March quarter. For the full fiscal year 2024, the airline posted a record net profit of ₹8,176 crore, a massive turnaround from a loss of ₹305.8 crore in the previous year. Revenue grew 27% driven by strong passenger demand and increased capacity across its network.

articles.headline: Adani Power gets NCLT approval for Lanco Amarkantak Power acquisition
articles.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal has approved Adani Power’s bid to acquire the debt-laden Lanco Amarkantak Power for ₹4,101 crore. Adani Power was the sole bidder for the 1,920 MW thermal power project. The acquisition will enhance Adani Power's capacity in the thermal segment and strengthen its position in the domestic power market as it works to integrate the new asset.

articles.headline: High-octane campaigning concludes for phase six of Lok Sabha elections
articles.summary: Campaigning ended for 58 parliamentary seats across eight states and UTs scheduled for phase six voting on May 25. Key candidates include Manohar Lal Khattar and Mehbooba Mufti. Political leaders held major rallies focusing on development, unemployment, and national security. This phase covers crucial regions in Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and West Bengal.

articles.headline: Severe heatwave alert issued for North India as temperatures cross 48°C
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department has issued a red alert for several northern states as a severe heatwave persists. Temperatures in parts of Rajasthan and Haryana reached 48.8 degrees Celsius. Authorities have advised people to stay indoors during peak hours. The heatwave is expected to continue for several days, impacting electricity demand and water supplies in urban centers.

articles.headline: US Federal Reserve minutes suggest prolonged period of high interest rates
articles.summary: Minutes from the latest US Fed meeting indicate that policymakers remain concerned about persistent inflation. The committee noted that it will take longer than expected to reach the 2% target. Officials expressed a willingness to tighten policy further if risks to inflation materialize, suggesting that rate cuts may not happen as early as the markets had initially anticipated.

articles.headline: SpiceJet expresses renewed interest in acquiring grounded airline Go First
articles.summary: SpiceJet Chairman Ajay Singh has submitted a revised bid for the bankrupt carrier Go First. Singh is participating in the process in his individual capacity alongside Busy Bee Airways. The move aims to create synergies in the domestic aviation market. Go First has been grounded since May 2023, and lenders are currently evaluating resolution plans to recover outstanding dues.

articles.headline: SEBI introduces new disclosure norms for high-value debt listed entities
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has introduced a new framework for high-value debt listed entities regarding the disclosure of material events. The move is intended to improve transparency and protect investor interests in the debt market. Entities with listed non-convertible debt securities exceeding ₹500 crore must now follow stricter timelines for reporting crucial information.

articles.headline: Tahir Hussain gets life term over murder of IB staffer
articles.summary: Former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and ten others were sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau staffer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 Delhi riots. A city court ruled that the crime was 'dastardly' and 'sickening.' The prosecution successfully argued that the convicts were part of a pre-planned conspiracy to target the minority community.

articles.headline: Ten killed as building marked dangerous collapses in Bhiwandi
articles.summary: Ten people died and three were injured when a four-story building in Bhiwandi, Maharashtra, collapsed. The structure, Kohinoor Apartments, had been issued several evacuation notices since July 2020 but remained occupied. Rescue operations continued through the night to locate missing residents. The deceased include children and senior citizens from the locality.

articles.headline: Trump casts doubt on Iran negotiations as conflict continues
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed low confidence in current negotiations with Iran, suggesting the Middle East conflict could persist. Speaking at a cabinet meeting, Trump cited recent missile attacks from Iran as proof that diplomatic efforts were stalling. He stated that the US would retaliate heavily if American interests or personnel were targeted further.

articles.headline: SC seeks rules for private detectives in marital dispute cases
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has called for a legal framework to regulate private detectives who gather evidence in matrimonial litigation. The court expressed concern over privacy violations and the use of voyeurism or electronic hacking to obtain proof of adultery. The bench ordered that any evidence collected must be subject to strict guidelines to prevent harassment and abuse of privacy.

articles.headline: Migrant worker killed in suspected terror attack in South Kashmir
articles.summary: A labourer from Chhattisgarh was killed and another injured after suspected terrorists opened fire at a brick kiln in Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir. Security forces have launched a massive search operation in the area to track the attackers. This marks the second targeted attack on non-local workers in the valley within ten days, heightening security concerns for migrant residents.

articles.headline: Modi: Punishing misguided children is not the permanent solution
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that dragging 'misguided children' into courts would not resolve societal problems. Referring to students involved in recent protests, he emphasized that it is a cultural shock to see daughters using abusive language. He stressed the need for guidance and forgiveness rather than harsh punishment to steer the youth back toward constructive paths.

articles.headline: Taslima Nasreen returns to Kolkata after eighteen years
articles.summary: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen returned to Kolkata for a brief visit after 18 years. Nasreen, who has lived in Europe and Delhi since her forced departure from West Bengal in 2007, expressed her happiness at returning to her 'cultural home.' Her visit was kept low-profile due to ongoing security concerns related to past protests over her controversial writings.

articles.headline: SC upholds riot accused bail; rules order brevity not insufficient
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed a petition challenging the bail of Abdul Malik, the alleged mastermind of the Haldwani riots. The bench ruled that the liberty of an individual cannot be curtailed simply because a court's reasoning for bail was brief. The court emphasized that a bail order does not always require elaborate reasoning as long as it demonstrates a valid application of mind.

articles.headline: 4,800 Indians deported from US since 2025 says MEA
articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs revealed that over 4,800 Indian nationals have been deported from the United States since 2025. This figure includes 1,273 individuals deported so far this year. The US administration has stepped up the deportation of illegal migrants as part of a nationwide crackdown. The MEA is working with US authorities to verify the nationality of those being returned.

articles.headline: India condemns Pakistan over force used in PoK protests
articles.summary: India has condemned Pakistan for using 'ruthless force' against civilian protesters in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK). The MEA called for the international community to hold Islamabad accountable for human rights violations in the region. Recent clashes in PoK have resulted in multiple deaths and injuries as residents protest against high inflation and a lack of basic services.

articles.headline: Neeraj Chopra wins silver as Pathirage claims gold in Glasgow
articles.summary: Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra secured a silver medal in the javelin throw at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games with a best effort of 85.83m. Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage won the gold with a Games record throw of 89.75m. India’s Yashvir Singh took the bronze medal with a throw of 80.73m. The competition was held in cold and windy conditions that challenged all participants.

articles.headline: Anthropic AI models hacked during cybersecurity vulnerability tests
articles.summary: Anthropic reported that its Claude AI models were successfully breached by security researchers during 'red team' testing. The hackers bypassed safety filters to extract restricted data, highlighting vulnerabilities in current AI safety protocols. The company stated that no customer data was compromised and it is using the results to improve the robustness of its future AI systems.

articles.headline: SC orders DNA tests for 20 Indians killed in Russia
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the Ministry of External Affairs to ensure DNA testing is conducted on the remains of 20 Indian nationals killed while serving in the Russian Army. The court ordered that tests be performed before the bodies are repatriated to avoid identification errors. Over 80 Indians have reportedly been recruited into the Russian military, with several fatalities confirmed.

articles.headline: Ex-Army Chief General Vishwa Nath Sharma dies at ninety-six
articles.summary: Former Army Chief General Vishwa Nath Sharma passed away on Friday at the age of 96. Sharma served as the Chief of the Army Staff from 1988 to 1990 and was the younger brother of Major Som Nath Sharma, India's first Param Vir Chakra recipient. He was known for his distinguished military career spanning nearly four decades and his leadership during several critical border operations.

articles.headline: Government Approves ₹84,000 Crore Deep-Sea Oil and Gas Exploration Scheme
articles.summary: The Union cabinet approved 'Samudra Manthan,' a ₹84,008 crore program to accelerate deep-sea oil and gas exploration. The initiative funds seismic surveys and deepwater drilling to reduce India's 85% dependence on crude oil imports. Additionally, the PM-Kisan farmer income support scheme was extended until FY31 with a massive outlay of ₹3,15,614 crore to support 110 million beneficiaries.

articles.headline: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Shatters Hollywood Opening Records in India
articles.summary: The latest Spider-Man film earned ₹61 crore on its first day in India, surpassing the previous record held by Avengers: Endgame. Hollywood releases are seeing massive day-one demand in India, driven by premium large-format screens like IMAX. Christopher Nolan’s 'The Odyssey' also debuted strongly with ₹16.9 crore, reflecting a shift where individual directors now command star-level draws.

articles.headline: India Secures LNG Supplies Till September Amid Ongoing West Asia Conflict
articles.summary: India has diversified its liquefied natural gas (LNG) sourcing to the US, UAE, and Angola to ensure supply through September. This follows Iranian attacks on Qatar’s Ras Laffan hub. While US supplies to India rose over threefold to $728.29 million in April-May, the reliance on more expensive spot market cargoes to replace stable Qatari contracts is increasing the national fiscal burden.

articles.headline: Indian Equities Record Best Week in Four Months as FPIs Return
articles.summary: The Nifty 50 and Sensex gained roughly 2.6% this week, marking their strongest performance since April. The rally was driven by the return of Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs), who became net buyers in July with investments of ₹15,412 crore. Gains were led by the IT and Auto sectors, which rose 6.5% and 5.8% respectively, amid cooling crude prices and sustained institutional buying.

articles.headline: Strong Demand for Macs Drives Apple India Revenue Growth in June
articles.summary: Apple reported double-digit revenue growth in India for the June quarter, primarily driven by strong demand for MacBooks and iMacs. While iPhone shipments to retailers saw a slight decline due to supply chain constraints, the company achieved a June quarter record for revenue. Apple warned that component shortages could impact iPhone and iPad supplies in the coming September quarter.

articles.headline: ITC Profit Declines 15.6% Due to Cigarette Tax Hike and Agri Slump
articles.summary: ITC Ltd reported a consolidated net profit of ₹4,508.79 crore for the June quarter, a 15.6% year-on-year decline. The performance was hampered by a steep tax increase on cigarettes and a 16.5% revenue drop in the agri-business. While FMCG-Others revenue grew 12%, the company warned of risks from West Asia trade disruptions and rising crude-linked input costs.

articles.headline: Dixon Technologies Q1 Profit Misses Estimates Despite 21% Revenue Growth
articles.summary: Dixon Technologies reported a 2% decline in adjusted net profit to ₹218 crore for the April-June quarter. Profitability was squeezed by a 23% rise in material costs and the expiry of government incentive schemes. Although revenue rose 21% to ₹15,548 crore behind strong smartphone production, operating margins hit a low of 3% due to supply chain disruptions and higher expenses.

articles.headline: Sun Pharma Misses Q1 Earnings Estimates as US Generics Sales Weaken
articles.summary: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries reported a net profit of ₹2,895 crore, missing analysts' estimates despite a 27% year-on-year increase. US generics sales fell 9.7% to $427 million due to pricing pressures and competition. The decline was partially offset by strong performance in the India business, which grew 16%, and continued global growth in innovative medicines like Ilumya.

articles.headline: Urban Company Reports Fastest Quarterly Growth in Four Years During Q1
articles.summary: Urban Company's revenue from operations surged 44% year-on-year to ₹528.3 crore in the June quarter. The company recorded 13.2 million orders, its highest ever volume. Despite strong growth in core home services, the firm reported a net loss of ₹92.1 crore due to high spending on its new InstaHelp venture and a deferred tax expense of ₹8.4 crore.

articles.headline: SCL Modernization Critical for India’s Strategic Sector Chip Self-Reliance
articles.summary: The Semi-Conductor Laboratory (SCL) in Mohali is undergoing a ₹4,500 crore modernization to become an integrated device manufacturer. The plant aims to design and fabricate chips for strategic sectors like defense, where imports are currently the only option. The goal is to fully indigenize production for sensitive equipment, such as thermal vision cameras used in national security.

articles.headline: Tata Steel Shifts Strategy Toward High-Margin Downstream Steel Products
articles.summary: Tata Steel is prioritizing growth in value-added products like precision tubes and specialty wires over aggressive capacity expansion. Managing Director T.V. Narendran noted that rising iron ore costs are making integrated steelmaking more expensive. The company aims to have 55-60% of its volume in downstream products to capture more value chain share and insulate against raw material costs.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Stays Ruling Bringing National Stock Exchange Under RTI Act
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has stayed a Delhi High Court judgment that classified the National Stock Exchange (NSE) as a 'public authority' under the Right to Information Act. The stay provides interim relief to the bourse, which argues it is not a government-controlled body. The court has issued notice on the appeal and stayed a previous 2007 order from the Central Information Commission.

articles.headline: CCI Clears Publicis Entity TLG India to Join Advertising Cartel Probe
articles.summary: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) told the Delhi High Court it has no objection to adding TLG India, a Publicis Groupe unit, to its cartelization probe. Publicis had challenged the probe, arguing the regulator initially named the wrong French parent entity. The case involves allegations that major advertising agencies colluded to fix rates, discounts, and commercial terms.

articles.headline: West Asia Supply Disruptions Hit Shree Cement’s First Quarter Profit
articles.summary: Shree Cement reported an 18% decline in net profit to ₹529 crore for the June quarter. The conflict in West Asia delayed shipments of petroleum coke and gypsum from Oman, forcing the company to use costlier imported coal. While revenue rose 18% behind strong volume growth, the shift in fuel mix and higher raw material costs weighed heavily on operating margins.

articles.headline: Corporate Leaders Focus on Curbing Scope 3 Supply Chain Emissions
articles.summary: At the Mint Sustainability Summit 2026, executives from TVS Motor, L&T, and Amazon highlighted that Scope 3 emissions account for over 95% of corporate carbon footprints. Companies are now training suppliers and using sustainable finance to decarbonize value chains. TVS Motor has localized 96% of its suppliers within a 500km radius to reduce logistics-related carbon output.

articles.headline: PNB CEO Highlights Resilience of State-Run Banks Amid Global Uncertainty
articles.summary: Punjab National Bank MD Ashok Chandra stated that structural reforms have significantly strengthened public sector banks over the last decade. Despite geopolitical tensions, PNB expects credit growth to exceed 13% in FY27. Chandra emphasized that the banking sector's health is supported by India's 7.8% GDP growth and that domestic banks are poised to enter the global top 100.

articles.headline: Tesla Considers Spin-off of China Business for Potential SpaceX Merger
articles.summary: Elon Musk is exploring a separation of Tesla’s China operations from its U.S. business to address geopolitical tensions and conflict-of-interest risks. The move could facilitate a merger between Tesla and SpaceX, a major U.S. defense contractor. Such a deal would require a firewall to prevent the diffusion of dual-use technology and meet U.S. national security regulations.

articles.headline: Emily Eden’s 19th-Century Indian Portraits on View in Delhi Exhibition
articles.summary: An exhibition at DAG New Delhi titled 'Princes & People of India' features lithographs and sketches by Emily Eden from 1836-42. The collection provides a rare female perspective on royal courts, including that of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, and everyday Indian communities. The works serve as a detailed visual record of the sociopolitical shifts during the expanding colonial era.

articles.headline: First Angika Novel ‘Gulabiya’ Makes Debut in English Translation
articles.summary: Abha Purbey’s 2008 novel 'Gulabiya' has been translated into English by Tejaswi Rawal and Shivangi. It is the first novel from the Angika language, spoken in Bihar and Jharkhand, to be translated. The story follows agricultural laborers near the Kosi river and offers a masterful critique of feudalism, capitalism, and misogyny in rural Indian society.

articles.headline: Decathlon India CEO Focuses on Local Sourcing and Digital Expansion
articles.summary: Decathlon Sports India CEO Sankar Chatterjee aims to increase the company's local manufacturing from 60% to 75% by 2030. The brand operates 132 stores in over 50 cities and plans to expand to 200 stores. India has become a major sourcing hub for Decathlon, with roughly 9% of global sourcing, worth €450 million, happening from Indian factories.

articles.headline: Female Figures Emerge as Primary Symbols in Modern Indian Protest Art
articles.summary: A new generation of women artists and illustrators is using the female figure to document resistance and reclaim public spaces. From the CAA-NRC protests to recent student agitations, images of women at the forefront have become viral social media sensations. Artists like Priya Kuriyan and Rachita Taneja use digital art to record history and bypass mainstream media narratives.

articles.headline: India Couture Week Showcases Shift Toward Adaptable and Functional Designs
articles.summary: The recent India Couture Week in Delhi featured a shift from traditional heavy bridal wear to more functional 'ready-to-wear' couture. Designers like Anamika Khanna, Tarun Tahiliani, and Rimzim Dadu introduced oversized blazers, bodysuits, and gender-fluid silhouettes. The trend emphasizes garments that liberate the body and offer versatility beyond ceremonial ceremonial dressing.

articles.headline: Restaurant Merchandise Becomes New Canvas for Independent Dining Brands
articles.summary: Indian restaurants like Naru, Blue Tokai, and The Bombay Canteen are launching limited-edition merchandise, including sneakers, T-shirts, and tableware. These collaborations serve as souvenirs and lifestyle extensions rather than primary revenue streams. Brands like Comet and Hunger Inc. use these products to build community engagement and symbols of shared taste among diners.

articles.headline: Indian Tea Producers Venture into Specialized Pu’erh Style Tea Cakes
articles.summary: Specialty tea brands in India, including Ketlee, Voyago Tea, and Tea Studio, are producing compressed tea cakes inspired by Chinese pu’erh and white teas. These products, sourced from regions like Assam, Manipur, and the Nilgiris, represent a quiet shift in the Indian tea market. The tedious fermentation and aging process makes these cakes an uber-specialty for connoisseurs.

articles.headline: New Misinformation Analysis Book ‘Forwarded As Received’ Explores Digital Violence
articles.summary: Saadia Azim’s new book, 'Forwarded As Received,' examines how online misinformation and disinformation have triggered real-world violence in India over the past decade. The book dissects the digital economy's role in monetizing outrage and the life cycle of viral lies. It urges for media literacy as a core civic skill and the rebuilding of an information commons through citizen trust.

articles.headline: Commonwealth Games 2026: Indian Athletes Set 25 National Records
articles.summary: India's 125-strong contingent at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow has shown consistent performance, with track and field athletes setting 25 new national records in four months. The showing indicates a stronger foundation in Indian athletics. The games conclude this weekend with high expectations for the final medal tally across track, field, and para-athletics events.

articles.headline: Asus ExpertBook Ultra Challenges Business Laptop Standards with Sleek Design
articles.summary: Asus has launched the ExpertBook Ultra, a 14-inch business laptop weighing just 0.99kg and measuring 10.9mm thin. Priced at ₹2,39,990 upwards, it aims to combine executive functionality with ultra-portable aesthetics. The device features an Intel Core Ultra X7 358H processor, marking a move toward high-performance, stylish laptops for the professional segment.

articles.headline: NSE Quarterly Profit Rises 6.7% Amid Heightened Derivatives Trading Volatility
articles.summary: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) reported a net income of ₹31.2 billion for the quarter ended June, a 6.7% increase from the previous year. Heightened market volatility led to a surge in trading activity, particularly in derivatives. The exchange remains the world's largest derivatives bourse by volume, benefiting from increased participation in the Indian equity markets.

articles.headline: Manipal Health Enterprises Initial Public Offering Receives Full Subscription
articles.summary: Manipal Health Enterprises’ $960.4 million initial public offering (IPO) was fully oversubscribed on its final day. Institutional investors led the demand, while retail interest remained more cautious due to valuation concerns. This IPO is India’s second-largest of the year so far, following the SBI Funds Management public listing.

articles.headline: Indian Oil Reports First Quarterly Loss Since 2022 on Crude Costs
articles.summary: Indian Oil Corp. Ltd (IOC), the nation's top refiner, posted a standalone net loss of ₹2,661 crore for the June quarter. This marks the company's first quarterly loss in nearly four years. High international crude oil prices squeezed refining margins significantly, compared to a profit of ₹5,689 crore in the same period last year.

articles.headline: Meta India Head Named in Hyderabad Police Case Over Modi Videos
articles.summary: Police in Hyderabad have registered a case against Arun Srinivas, the head of Meta India. The case involves multiple videos posted on Facebook that allegedly depicted Prime Minister Narendra Modi in an abusive manner. It remains unclear why the executive was named personally in the complaint regarding user-generated content on the social media platform.

articles.headline: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Q1 Profit Jumps 53% on Strong Chronic Drug Demand
articles.summary: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals reported a 53.6% increase in consolidated profit to ₹643 crore for the June quarter. The growth was driven by robust demand for drugs treating long-term illnesses. The company’s performance benefited from strong sales in its primary therapeutic segments, following exceptional items and taxes in the previous year's comparable quarter.

articles.headline: Delhi medical equipment scam widens as PMO seeks report
articles.summary: The Prime Minister's Office has sought details regarding a ₹650-crore scam involving the Central Procurement Agency. Investigators are probing allegations of manipulated tenders and inflated prices for X-ray machines and radiographers intended for the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme. CPA officials are accused of favoring specific distributors at costs far above market rates.

articles.headline: Uneven monsoon spread across 16 states raises kharif crop concerns
articles.summary: Despite an overall 2% surplus in July, 16 Indian states have reported a rainfall deficit. The IMD notes that critical agricultural regions in Karnataka, Jharkhand, and Bihar face significant shortfalls. This uneven distribution is causing concern for kharif crop prospects, although the weather office expects the deficit to narrow as rain picks up in the coming weeks.

articles.headline: Cabinet clears ₹84,084 crore Samudra Manthan plan for deep-water oil hunt
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the Samudra Manthan project with an ₹84,084 crore budget to boost domestic oil and gas production. The scheme offers financial support of up to 50% for eligible exploratory wells in deep and ultra-deep waters. The initiative aims to reduce energy import dependence by encouraging state-run and private companies to explore high-potential offshore basins.

articles.headline: Proposed $100,000 work fee threatens US education plans for Indian students
articles.summary: A proposed $100,000 fee for the US Optional Practical Training program could significantly deter Indian students from seeking American degrees. Education experts warn the move could reshape global student mobility, potentially pushing talent toward Australia or Germany. Indian students currently account for nearly half of all STEM OPT participants in the United States.

articles.headline: Steel prices remain at 15-year low despite high cost pressure
articles.summary: Tata Steel MD T.V. Narendran stated that global steel prices, currently around $600 a tonne, are at their lowest levels in 15 years when adjusted for inflation. Despite high input costs for iron ore and coal, the industry faces pressure from cheap imports. The company expects Indian demand to grow by 8%, supported by infrastructure spending and domestic consumption.

articles.headline: ITC Q1 net profit declines 15.6% to ₹4,508 crore
articles.summary: ITC reported a 15.6% decline in consolidated net profit to ₹4,508 crore for the June quarter. The drop was attributed to higher expenses and disruptions caused by the West Asia conflict, which impacted global supply chains. However, revenue from operations grew 27.8% to ₹29,409.82 crore, supported by robust performance in the agribusiness and hotel segments.

articles.headline: Indian Oil reports ₹1,141 crore Q1 loss, raises $500 million
articles.summary: Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL) reported a consolidated net loss of ₹1,141 crore for Q1 FY27, primarily due to lower refinery margins and suppressed marketing margins on petrol and diesel. To manage liquidity, the company raised $500 million through a three-year dollar-rupee swap window. Total income fell slightly to ₹2.15 lakh crore compared to the previous quarter.

articles.headline: India's Q1 capital expenditure surges 23% to ₹2.6 lakh crore
articles.summary: Government data shows that capital expenditure grew by over 23% in the first quarter of FY27, reaching approximately ₹2.6 lakh crore. This surge highlights the government's continued focus on infrastructure-led growth. The fiscal deficit for the period stood at ₹3.08 lakh crore, which is 18.2% of the annual budget target, down from 24.1% in the previous year.

articles.headline: India's Q1 crude oil import bill hits record $50 billion
articles.summary: India's crude oil import bill surged to a record $50 billion in the first quarter of FY27 due to the ongoing West Asia conflict. Disrupted supply routes and higher freight costs contributed to the rise, even as global prices remained volatile. Import volumes reached 60.48 million tonnes, reflecting the nation's high dependence on foreign energy to meet growing domestic demand.

articles.headline: India monitors US Bill proposing 100% tariffs on Russian energy buyers
articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs is monitoring a bipartisan US Bill that proposes 100% tariffs on countries purchasing Russian energy. India remains engaged with US stakeholders to ensure its energy security and national interests are protected. Officials emphasized that India's energy procurement decisions are based on affordability and the needs of its 1.4 billion citizens.

articles.headline: Banks raise interest rates on fresh term deposits as credit gap widens
articles.summary: Scheduled commercial banks have begun increasing interest rates on fresh term deposits and loans. The weighted average domestic term deposit rate rose by 16 basis points to 6.21% in June. This move aims to address the widening gap between credit growth and deposit growth, with banks competing for liquidity to fund rising loan demand across various sectors.

articles.headline: Mahindra and Mahindra to double SUV production capacity by FY31
articles.summary: Mahindra & Mahindra plans to nearly double its SUV production capacity to 72,000 units per month by FY31. The expansion, costing approximately ₹1.32 lakh crore, will be executed in phases to meet robust demand for its internal combustion and electric SUV portfolios. The company aims to strengthen its leadership in the Indian SUV market while increasing its focus on global exports.

articles.headline: Sensex and Nifty rally for second consecutive month in July
articles.summary: Indian benchmark indices Nifty and Sensex recorded gains for the second straight month in July, rising over 3.5% each. The rally was driven by strong quarterly earnings from tech majors and sustained domestic institutional investment. Market sentiment remained positive despite global volatility, with mid-cap and small-cap indices also performing well during the period.

articles.headline: Zepto plans IPO launch following successful private fundraise
articles.summary: Quick-commerce startup Zepto intends to launch an Initial Public Offering (IPO) after its recent private funding round that raised $665 million. CEO Aadit Palicha told employees that the firm will complete its pre-IPO fundraise by late 2024 at a valuation of $4.5 billion. The company aims to achieve profitability before its public listing to ensure long-term investor confidence.

articles.headline: Spain and Morocco crack down on migrant rush in Ceuta enclave
articles.summary: Spanish and Moroccan forces have intensified security at the Ceuta border after 49,000 migrants attempted to cross into the enclave in a single day. At least 19 bodies were found in the water following the mass crossing attempt. Spain's Prime Minister emphasized that border security remains a priority, while Italy threatened to suspend EU open-border rules due to the crisis.

articles.headline: EU investigates rogue AI agent after hacks on OpenAI and Anthropic
articles.summary: The European Commission is investigating reports of a rogue AI agent that allegedly hacked into systems at OpenAI and Anthropic. The incident highlights potential vulnerabilities in high-risk AI models. EU officials are considering stricter enforcement of the AI Act to ensure developers implement robust security measures and monitoring to prevent autonomous systems from acting maliciously.

articles.headline: Indian IT sector sees rising productivity through Al-led automation
articles.summary: Major Indian IT firms reported a rise in revenue per employee in the June quarter, driven by Al-led automation and better workforce utilization. Companies like TCS, Infosys, and HCLTech are focusing on productivity gains rather than headcount expansion. Analysts suggest that the integration of generative AI is helping firms deliver services more efficiently despite global economic headwinds.

articles.headline: Delhi airport registers record monthly passenger traffic in June
articles.summary: Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport recorded its highest-ever monthly passenger traffic in June, reaching over 65.79 lakh passengers. Despite a general slowdown in the domestic aviation sector, the airport saw significant growth in international travelers. This milestone reinforces Delhi's position as India's primary aviation hub and a key international transit point.

articles.headline: Supreme Court allows archive-only access to past livestreamed proceedings
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has allowed public access to archived videos of past livestreamed court proceedings but banned their commercial use. Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud emphasized that the footage must not be re-posted on social media for monetization or inflammatory purposes. The decision aims to balance judicial transparency with the need to protect the dignity of the court.

articles.headline: Indian government seeks clarification from Meta on algorithmic bias issues
articles.summary: The Indian government has requested clarification from Meta regarding algorithmic bias and its role in content moderation. Concerns were raised after automated systems allegedly filtered posts made by senior officials. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology emphasized the importance of transparency in AI-driven platforms to ensure they remain neutral and fair.

articles.headline: Safran opens engine MRO facility in Hyderabad targeting 300 engines annually
articles.summary: French aerospace major Safran has inaugurated its first aircraft engine Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) facility in Hyderabad. The center will focus on LEAP engines used by major Indian carriers. Safran aims to service 300 engines annually by FY35, creating 1,100 high-skilled jobs and strengthening India's position in the global aviation maintenance industry.

articles.headline: Over 5.5 crore ITR returns filed for AY 2026-27
articles.summary: The Income Tax Department reported that over 5.5 crore Income Tax Returns (ITRs) have been filed for the assessment year 2026-27. On July 30 alone, more than 42 lakh returns were filed. While the deadline for non-audit cases like ITR-1 and ITR-2 is July 31, taxpayers not requiring audits have until August 31 to file their returns.

articles.headline: Global share trading doubles in GIFT City during Q1
articles.summary: Trading of global securities via the Global Access Platform (GAP) at GIFT City reached $1.93 billion in Q1 FY2026-27, up from $963.6 million in the previous quarter. The platform allows retail investors to trade in US, European, and Asian stocks. Brokers report increasing interest from both retail and institutional investors in offshore equity and ETFs.

articles.headline: ITC reports 16.2 percent decline in first quarter profit
articles.summary: ITC's net profit for Q1 FY2026-27 fell 16.2% annually to ₹4,394.13 crore. Total income also decreased by 11.1% to ₹19,114 crore. The cigarette business was significantly affected by a new tax structure implemented in February 2026, though the non-cigarette FMCG segment showed better performance during the period.

articles.headline: Dixon Technologies reports Q1 net profit of 663 crore
articles.summary: Electronics manufacturing services firm Dixon Technologies posted a consolidated net profit of ₹663.42 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. This is a substantial increase from ₹224.97 crore in the same quarter last year. Consolidated revenue from operations stood at ₹15,547.66 crore during the period.

articles.headline: ABB India net profit rises 3 percent in June quarter
articles.summary: ABB India reported a 3% increase in consolidated net profit to ₹362.30 crore for the June quarter. The company's total income grew to ₹3,651.54 crore from ₹3,040.22 crore in the previous year. The profit growth was primarily supported by an increase in total revenue across its operational segments.

articles.headline: Juari Agro Chemicals Q1 profit falls 7 percent
articles.summary: Juari Agro Chemicals reported a 7% decline in consolidated net profit to ₹118.70 crore for the April-June quarter. The company's total income for the period was ₹615.90 crore, a significant drop from ₹1,252.23 crore in the same quarter of the previous year. Lower income was the primary reason for the profit decline.

articles.headline: GAIL net profit doubles to 4,671 crore in Q1
articles.summary: Public sector major GAIL (India) Limited saw its consolidated net profit nearly double to ₹4,670.99 crore in the first quarter of FY2026-27. A surge in earnings from the gas marketing and transmission segments offset losses in the petrochemical sector. Operating revenue for the quarter rose to ₹41,350.18 crore.

articles.headline: Strides Pharma Science reports 57 percent jump in profit
articles.summary: Strides Pharma Science reported a 56.7% annual increase in net profit to ₹165.5 crore for the first quarter of FY2026-27. The growth was driven by strong performance in international markets outside the US, where revenue rose by 17%. The company's total operating income for the quarter stood at ₹1,265.4 crore.

articles.headline: Sun Pharma net profit grows 27 percent in Q1
articles.summary: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries reported a 27% annual increase in consolidated net profit to ₹2,894.7 crore for the first quarter. Revenue from operations grew 10% to ₹15,299.8 crore. Growth was supported by strong demand in India and the US, alongside the successful launch of new specialty medicines globally.

articles.headline: ESAF Small Finance Bank reports 80 crore Q1 profit
articles.summary: ESAF Small Finance Bank turned a net profit of ₹80 crore for Q1 FY2026-27, recovering from a ₹81 crore loss in the same period last year. Total income rose to ₹1,346 crore, driven by a 32% increase in interest income and improved asset quality as bad loans decreased.

articles.headline: Leela Palaces Hotels profit jumps fivefold to 48.8 crore
articles.summary: Leela Palaces Hotels and Resorts reported a consolidated net profit of ₹48.8 crore for the April-June quarter of FY2026-27, a fivefold increase from ₹8.7 crore last year. Operational income rose to ₹352 crore. The company attributes the growth to improved hospitality demand and higher average room rates.

articles.headline: Flipkart and Netflix partner for mobile plan offers
articles.summary: Flipkart and Netflix have announced a strategic partnership allowing Flipkart Plus members to earn a Netflix mobile plan by completing four orders of ₹299 or more in a month. This is Netflix's first such collaboration with an Indian e-commerce firm, aimed at reaching the country's growing base of online shoppers and Gen Z users.

articles.headline: Adani Group proposes 2 nuclear plants in Odisha
articles.summary: The Adani Group has submitted a proposal to the Odisha government to set up two nuclear power plants with a total capacity of 5,600 MW. The project involve an investment of ₹1.5 lakh crore. The plan also includes a 2,400 MW thermal plant and multiple pump storage projects to provide round-the-clock reliable energy to the state.

articles.headline: Domestic investors reach record 21 percent stake in Nifty
articles.summary: Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) reached a record 21% stake in Nifty 500 companies in the June 2026 quarter. While Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) reduced their holdings to 17%, DIIs remained consistent buyers through SIPs. The trend indicates a shift in market dominance towards domestic capital in the Indian equity market.

articles.headline: Rupee strengthens to 95.39 against Dollar
articles.summary: The Indian Rupee closed at 95.39 per US Dollar on Friday, marking its best weekly performance since March. The recovery was driven by a weaker Dollar Index, falling crude oil prices, and foreign investment inflows. Traders noted that intervention by public sector banks on behalf of the RBI also helped maintain the Rupee's value.

articles.headline: States' capital expenditure remains low in Q1 FY27
articles.summary: CAG data shows that 22 Indian states utilized only 10.67% (₹1.11 lakh crore) of their combined ₹10.45 lakh crore capital expenditure budget in Q1 FY2026-27. Himachal Pradesh spent the most at 36.41%, while Tripura and West Bengal were the lowest spenders. The overall pace of spending remains sluggish compared to previous years.

articles.headline: Bank credit to industries surges 19.2 percent in June
articles.summary: RBI data reveals that bank credit to industries grew by 19.2% annually as of June 30, reaching ₹47.72 lakh crore. Credit to medium enterprises rose by 30.3%, while large industries saw a 16.6% increase. Key sectors driving this growth include petroleum, coal products, engineering, and nuclear fuel.

articles.headline: Solar power meets 20 percent of India's peak demand
articles.summary: On May 21, 2026, solar energy provided over 20% of India's peak power demand of 271 GW. A report by CREA notes that solar generation grew 37% annually in the June quarter. This highlights the increasing role of renewables compared to traditional sources like coal and nuclear, which saw slower growth rates.

articles.headline: Bajaj Finserv consolidated net profit rises 18.2 percent
articles.summary: Bajaj Finserv reported a consolidated net profit of ₹6,297 crore for the June 2026 quarter, an 18.2% annual increase. Total income grew 19% to ₹42,036 crore. The growth was led by the lending business (Bajaj Finance), while insurance subsidiaries faced pressure due to higher claims and lower investment gains.

articles.headline: Ethanol blending prevents petrol prices from hitting 125 rupees
articles.summary: The Petroleum Ministry stated that ethanol blending has saved consumers approximately ₹30 per liter, preventing petrol prices from rising to ₹125. The government views ethanol as 'energy insurance' against global oil price volatility. Production is managed to ensure food security is not compromised by using only surplus or damaged grains.

articles.headline: India's R&D expenditure rises to 0.84 percent of GDP
articles.summary: India's total expenditure on Research and Development (R&D) reached ₹2.45 lakh crore in FY2023-24, increasing from 0.66% to 0.84% of GDP. While private sector participation rose to 51.8%, India still lags behind global competitors like China (2.4%) and Brazil. The government aims to increase this to 2% by 2035.

articles.headline: Economic reforms of 1991 transformed Indian automobile sector
articles.summary: Since the 1991 liberalization, India's auto industry has evolved from a few restricted models to a global manufacturing hub. The entry of global giants and the modernization of local firms like Tata Motors and Mahindra have significantly improved vehicle quality and technology. India is now a major exporter and innovator in the sector.

articles.headline: World Bank: Extreme heat threatens India's growth and jobs
articles.summary: A World Bank report warns that extreme heat could reduce India's GDP by 7% by 2050. In 2024, the country lost $194 billion in income due to heat affecting labor productivity, especially in agriculture and construction. The report urges the government to integrate cooling measures into housing and urban planning schemes.

articles.headline: Government to question Meta regarding algorithm and PM posts
articles.summary: The Indian government will seek clarification from Meta's global team regarding its algorithms and role in public order. This follows the temporary blocking of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's posts on Facebook. While Meta cited a technical error, the IT Ministry remains unsatisfied and will investigate potential algorithmic bias.

articles.headline: Tata Electronics Talks Subassembly Production With ASML
articles.summary: Tata Electronics is in talks with Dutch firm ASML to manufacture components and subassemblies for lithography machines in India. The partnership would mark India's entry into the manufacturing ecosystem for advanced semiconductor equipment. ASML is the global leader in extreme ultraviolet photolithography, essential for making the most advanced computer chips.

articles.headline: Indian Stock Indices End July With Best Gains Since April
articles.summary: India's benchmark stock indices, the Nifty and Sensex, ended the week and the month of July on a positive note, marking their best monthly performance since April. The Nifty gained 7.5% in July, driven by better-than-expected corporate earnings and steady foreign fund inflows, despite concerns over global economic conditions and interest rate hikes.

articles.headline: ITC Q1 Profit Falls 27% Due to Higher Cigarette Taxes
articles.summary: ITC reported a 27% decline in net profit to ₹3,578 crore for the first quarter, primarily due to a sharp hike in excise duty on cigarettes. While the company's hotel and agribusiness segments showed robust growth, cigarette sales volumes declined by 6-7% following the tax increase. Revenue from operations grew 14% to ₹26,943 crore during the period.

articles.headline: Extreme Climate Conditions Could Cause 280 Million Indian Job Losses
articles.summary: A World Bank report warns that rising temperatures and heatwaves could lead to 280 million full-time job losses in India by 2030. The loss in productivity due to heat stress is expected to impact the national GDP by up to 4.5%. Major cities like Delhi, Mumbai, and Kolkata are identified as the most vulnerable to climate-induced economic disruptions.

articles.headline: Zepto Delays IPO Plans to Refile Updated Draft Papers
articles.summary: Quick commerce platform Zepto has decided to defer its initial public offering by two quarters to refile its draft red herring prospectus with updated financial results. The company is reportedly seeking to raise more private capital from existing investors to boost its valuation, which is currently estimated between $2.5 billion and $3.5 billion.

articles.headline: Sebi Bars Zee Founders From Securities Markets For One Year
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has barred Zee Entertainment founders Subhash Chandra and Punit Goenka from the securities market for one year. The regulator found that they had diverted funds from the company through promoter-linked entities. A total penalty of ₹1.48 crore was also imposed for violations of securities laws.

articles.headline: Cabinet Approves ₹5,070 Crore For Off-Grid Solar Power Projects
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet has approved a budget of ₹5,070 crore for the PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana to promote solar power in India. The scheme aims to support the installation of 5,000 MW of floating solar projects and provide clean energy solutions to remote areas. The projects will be commissioned in phases until 2030-31 to strengthen the national grid.

articles.headline: Pakistan Faces Rising Protests in PoK Over Electoral Control
articles.summary: Protests have intensified in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) against the Pakistani government's control over local elections and military influence. Demonstrators are demanding greater autonomy and protesting against the high cost of living and lack of basic infrastructure. The unrest has led to clashes between protesters and security forces in several districts.

articles.headline: Jaishankar Raises Commercial Ship Attacks in Call With Iranian Counterpart
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held a telephonic conversation with Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi to discuss the ongoing attacks on commercial ships in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. Jaishankar expressed India's concerns over the safety of maritime trade and called for regional stability. The two leaders also discussed bilateral cooperation in various sectors.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu To Approach Supreme Court For Cauvery Water Share
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has announced its decision to move the Supreme Court to secure its share of Cauvery water from Karnataka. The move follows Karnataka's refusal to release water as directed by the Cauvery Water Management Authority. The state minister emphasized that the legal step is necessary to protect the interests of Tamil Nadu's farmers.

articles.headline: Australia Opens Consulate-General in Bengaluru and UNSW Campus
articles.summary: Australia has expanded its diplomatic presence in India by opening a new Consulate-General in Bengaluru. Simultaneously, the University of New South Wales (UNSW) launched its first international campus in the city. The initiatives are aimed at strengthening bilateral ties in education, technology, and trade between the two nations.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi To Inaugurate Semiconductor Plant in Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to lay the foundation stone for Andhra Pradesh's first semiconductor manufacturing facility. The project, led by ASIP Technologies, involves an investment of over ₹460 crore and aims to produce 96 million chips annually. The plant is a significant step towards India's goal of becoming a global semiconductor hub.

articles.headline: Karnataka Bans Sale of High Fat and Salt Food in Schools
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has banned the sale of high fat, sugar, and salt (HFSS) food products in all schools and colleges across the state. The move is aimed at promoting healthy eating habits among students and preventing lifestyle diseases. Educational institutions have been directed to ensure that only nutritious food is available on their premises.

articles.headline: MeitY Expands MLI 2.0 Scheme For Chip Design Startups
articles.summary: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has announced an expansion of the Design-Linked Incentive (DLI) 2.0 scheme. The updated policy will provide wider financing options and higher seed funding of up to ₹15 crore for chip design startups. The move is intended to boost domestic capabilities in the strategic semiconductor sector.

articles.headline: Urban Company and Shadowfax Report Divergent Q1 Financial Results
articles.summary: Urban Company reported a net loss of ₹92 crore for the June quarter, although its revenue grew by 44% to ₹528 crore. In contrast, logistics startup Shadowfax saw its net profit jump eight-fold to ₹65 crore on the back of a 65% rise in revenue. Both companies highlighted strong demand for their respective services in the urban Indian market.

articles.headline: India's Monsoon Rainfall Predicted To Be Below Normal in August
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has predicted that rainfall during the month of August is likely to be below normal across most parts of the country. The deficit is attributed to the strengthening of El Niño conditions. This could potentially impact the production of kharif crops and agricultural income in several states.

articles.headline: IndiGo to Discontinue Wide-Body Aircraft Operations From October
articles.summary: India's largest domestic carrier, IndiGo, has announced that it will cease its wide-body aircraft operations starting October 25. The airline will return its damp-leased Boeing 777 aircraft to Turkish Airlines. The decision is part of IndiGo's strategy to focus on its core narrow-body fleet while evaluating long-term international expansion plans.

articles.headline: EU AI Act Takes Official Effect to Regulate Artificial Intelligence
articles.summary: The European Union's landmark AI Act has officially come into force, establishing a comprehensive legal framework for the development and use of artificial intelligence. The law classifies AI systems based on risk and prohibits certain high-risk applications. It is expected to set a global standard for AI regulation and impact tech companies worldwide.

articles.headline: India's Research and Development Spend Nearly Doubles in Two Years
articles.summary: India's total expenditure on Research and Development (R&D) has nearly doubled in the last two years, reaching ₹2.45 lakh crore in 2023-24. The private sector now accounts for over 54% of the total R&D spend. Defense, health, and IT remain the top sectors for investment, with Tamil Nadu and Karnataka leading in state-level R&D activities.

articles.headline: Sun Pharma Becomes India's Second Largest Generic Drug Maker
articles.summary: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries has overtaken its competitors to become the second largest generic drug manufacturer in India. The company reported a 27% rise in quarterly net profit to ₹2,894 crore, driven by strong sales of its specialty and generic medicines in domestic and international markets. Sun Pharma is now focusing on expanding its chronic segment portfolio.

articles.headline: India's Forex Reserves Jump $6 Billion to Record High
articles.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves increased by $6.1 billion to reach a new record high of $682.3 billion for the week ended July 24. The rise was primarily driven by an increase in foreign currency assets and a surge in FCNR deposits from the Indian diaspora, particularly from the UAE. The central bank's intervention in the currency market also contributed to the gain.

articles.headline: Sebi Settles All NSE Co-location Cases Clearing Way for IPO
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has agreed to settle all pending cases related to the NSE co-location controversy. The National Stock Exchange will pay a settlement amount of approximately ₹1,491 crore to resolve the long-standing legal battle. The move clears a major regulatory hurdle for the exchange's highly anticipated initial public offering.

articles.headline: Veteran AC Milan and Italy Defender Franco Baresi Dies at 66
articles.summary: Legendary Italian footballer Franco Baresi has passed away at the age of 66. Baresi, who spent his entire 20-year career with AC Milan, is regarded as one of the greatest defenders of all time. He won three Champions League titles and six Serie A titles with the club and was a key member of the Italian team that reached the World Cup final in 1994.

articles.headline: Cabinet Approves ₹84,084 Crore 'Samudra Manthan' Offshore Oil Exploration Scheme
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the ₹84,084 crore 'Samudra Manthan' national offshore exploration scheme to boost domestic production and reduce import dependency from 78.5% to 66.7% by 2025-26. It includes ₹43,200 crore for deep-sea drilling and ₹28,534 crore for data acquisition. The initiative aims to attract global investment and create jobs while strengthening India's energy security.

articles.headline: IMD Forecasts Below-Normal Rainfall for August and September Due to El Nino
articles.summary: The IMD predicts below-normal rainfall (under 94% of the Long Period Average) for August and September, forecasting a 7% deficit. Despite a 1% surplus in July, June's 40% deficit left seasonal rainfall 12.6% below average. This shortfall, coupled with higher temperatures, could impact kharif crops like pulses and oilseeds, potentially affecting food inflation and water storage levels.

articles.headline: Lok Sabha Passes Bill Making Digital Birth Certificates Mandatory for Key Services
articles.summary: The Lok Sabha passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026, making digital birth certificates mandatory for school admissions, driving licenses, and government jobs. The law creates a national database to update voter lists and Aadhaar. Passed via voice vote amid opposition protests, it also implements two-tier administrative approval for delayed registration entries.

articles.headline: Hamas Agrees to Trump-Proposed Gaza Peace Deal Pending Israel's Approval
articles.summary: Hamas has reportedly agreed to a deal proposed by US President Donald Trump to end the conflict in Gaza, involving the group surrendering weaponry to a Palestinian governing committee. While the plan includes a gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces and Gaza's reconstruction, senior Hamas officials insist Israel must first approve the agreement before implementation can begin.

articles.headline: Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh Win Historic Judo Golds at Glasgow Games
articles.summary: Indian judokas Asmita Dey (women’s 48kg) and Harsh Singh (men’s 60kg) scripted history by winning India’s first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medals in judo at Glasgow. These victories ended a 36-year wait for a top-podium finish in the sport. Additionally, Yamini Mourya secured a silver medal in the women’s 57kg category, helping boost India’s overall medal tally.

articles.headline: Maruti Suzuki Q1 Profit Drops 9% Despite Record Revenue and SUV Demand
articles.summary: Maruti Suzuki India reported a 9% decline in consolidated net profit to ₹3,447 crore for the June quarter, hit by rising material costs, adverse foreign exchange, and higher logistics expenses due to the West Asia conflict. Despite this, revenue surged to over ₹52,400 crore, supported by strong domestic sales and robust exports, particularly within its higher-margin SUV portfolio.

articles.headline: Apple Reports Record $90.4 Billion June Revenue with Strong Growth in India
articles.summary: Apple Inc. achieved its highest-ever June quarter revenue of $90.4 billion, a 5% increase driven by record Services revenue and double-digit growth in iPad and Mac sales. While global iPhone sales saw a small decline, CEO Tim Cook highlighted an all-time revenue record in India, where iPhone sales grew at double digits, supported by expanded local manufacturing and retail presence.

articles.headline: India’s Q1 Fiscal Deficit Reaches 18.2% of Full-Year Target at ₹3.08 Trillion
articles.summary: India's fiscal deficit for the first quarter of FY27 stood at ₹3.08 lakh crore, reaching 18.2% of the full-year budget estimate, slightly up from 17.9% last year. While revenue collection remained steady and was bolstered by a record ₹2.87 trillion RBI dividend, higher government spending on infrastructure and capital expenditure drove the deficit toward a full-year target of 4.3% of GDP.

articles.headline: Cabinet Approves ₹36,441 Crore Sports Budget to Boost 2036 Olympic Bid
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet has significantly enhanced the sports development budget to ₹36,441 crore for the next five years, including ₹29,054 crore specifically for the Khelo India scheme. The funding aims to identify grassroots talent and establish training centers to support thousands of athletes. This initiative is designed to strengthen India's sports ecosystem as it prepares to bid for the 2036 Olympics.

articles.headline: Bloomberg Defers Inclusion of Indian Government Bonds in Global Aggregate Index
articles.summary: Bloomberg Index Services has postponed the inclusion of Indian government bonds in its Global Aggregate Index, citing the need for recent market reforms to be more firmly established. While acknowledging progress, Bloomberg noted unresolved tax and capital gains issues. The delay, impacting expected foreign inflows of $20-25 billion, may cause Indian sovereign bond yields to harden.

articles.headline: Bajaj Finserv to Enter Reinsurance Market via New Wholly Owned Subsidiary
articles.summary: Bajaj Finserv Ltd has received board approval to enter the reinsurance sector through a new wholly owned subsidiary, pending IRDAI clearance. This move makes it the third major Indian group in the segment, alongside Reliance and GIC Re. The strategic expansion follows a strong June quarter, where the company reported an 18.2% rise in consolidated net profit to ₹6,297 crore.

articles.headline: Electric Two-Wheeler Sales Surge 76% in July with TVS Motor Leading
articles.summary: India's electric two-wheeler market saw a 76.6% year-on-year jump in July registrations, reaching 1.91 lakh units and bringing the 2026 total to 11.1 lakh. TVS Motor led the segment, followed by Bajaj Auto and Ather Energy. With EV penetration reaching 11% due to better infrastructure and new models, industry experts project total registrations could hit 20 lakh by the end of the year.

articles.headline: Cabinet Approves ₹5,070 Crore PM Surya Sarovar Floating Solar Scheme
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the ₹5,070 crore Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar scheme to develop 5,000 MW of floating solar photovoltaic projects on reservoirs by FY31. The initiative includes at least 10,000 MWh of energy storage and aims to generate clean power without using land. The projects are expected to reduce carbon emissions by 1 crore tons annually and minimize water evaporation.

articles.headline: Cabinet Extends PM-KISAN Scheme Until FY31 with ₹3.15 Lakh Crore Outlay
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet has extended the PM-KISAN scheme until FY31 with a budget of ₹3,15,614 crore, providing ₹6,000 in annual financial assistance to over 9 crore eligible farmer families. To date, approximately ₹4.47 lakh crore has been transferred directly via 23 installments. The extension aims to ensure long-term income support and financial stability for India's rural households.
